Topic 7.1: Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature, part of Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How does performance affect the subject matter in oral literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the features of a good performance for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. discuss qualities of a good story teller for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. evaluate performance techniques in oral literature for critical analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the place of performance in oral literature for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: This is nurtured as the learner interacts with digital content when searching online or offline for features of a

good performance and presents findings in class.

● Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when performing an oral

literature piece using the performance techniques.

Values:
● Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner gives honest and constructive feedback when reviewing each other’s performance

for creativity and correctness.

● Peace: This is advanced as the learner tolerates peers when watching the performance of any of the forms of oral literature

and identifying performance techniques applied.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills (self-awareness): This is nurtured as the learner exhibits individual skills and audience awareness to perform an oral

literature piece using performance techniques acquired.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the features of a good performance for information,
2. discuss qualities of a good story teller for literary appreciation,
3. evaluate performance techniques in oral literature for critical analysis,
4. acknowledge the place of performance in oral literature for lifelong learning.

Remember the key question: How does performance affect the subject matter in oral literature?
